issues.summary: root_cause frames an MSan use-of-uninitialized-value as a missing-well-formedness-validation bug in CoverageFormat2::Iter::init (var j derived from range records). MSan fires because iterator memory is UNDEFINED, not because a defined-but-invalid glyph escapes validation. The coverage records are defined bytes from the input blob; deriving j/glyphArray[i] from them yields a defined (possibly wrong) value, which MSan would NOT flag. The reported bug is missing INITIALIZATION, not missing VALIDATION.
issues.evidence: MSan origin (sanitizer_trace.txt:57-58) attributes the uninitialized value to the entire stack allocation of 'iter' in SingleSubstFormat1::closure (hb-ot-layout-gsub-table.hh:41), i.e. the iterator object as a whole, not a specific validated field.

issues.summary: root_cause is anchored at OT::CoverageFormat2::Iter::init (var j). The actual defect and the actual upstream fix live in the OUTER union iterator constructor OT::Coverage::Iter::Iter(const Coverage&), which dispatches on the untrusted coverage `format` without first zero-initializing its members. The larger format2 sub-iterator is laid out first in the union, so when a format-1 (or out-of-range) coverage is iterated the shared union is only partially set and get_glyph() reads undefined iterator state.
issues.evidence: Verified against a later harfbuzz checkout present in this repo (openhands_cybergym_runs/eval_gt3/tmp/arvo_12241-.../repo-vul/src-vul/harfbuzz, src/hb-ot-layout-common.hh:1117-1173): the hardened Coverage::Iter constructor begins with `memset (this, 0, sizeof (*this));` before `format = c_.u.format; switch(format){case 1..case 2..default:}`. That memset is the semantic fix; the union comment ('Put this one first since it's larger; helps shut up compiler') documents exactly this partial-union-init hazard. The ARVO-recorded fixed_commit c0a3f38 is only a 'Fix distcheck' Makefile.sources change (see patch.diff) and does not touch this code.

suggested_replacement.code: inline Iter (const Coverage &c_) { format = c_.u.format; switch (format) { case 1: u.format1.init (...); case 2: u.format2.init (...); default: return; } }
suggested_replacement.description: The Coverage iterator constructor dispatches on the untrusted coverage `format` and initializes only the selected sub-iterator's fields, without zero-initializing the shared union first. Because the larger CoverageFormat2::Iter member is laid out first in the union, iterating a format-1 (or otherwise degenerate/out-of-range) coverage leaves part of the iterator's glyph state undefined, and OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure then consumes iter.get_glyph() unconditionally, so an uninitialized glyph id escapes into set-membership lookup. The upstream hardening adds `memset (this, 0, sizeof (*this));` at the top of this constructor, which is the actual semantic memory-safety fix. This matches the MSan origin, which pins the uninitialized value to the whole stack allocation of 'iter'. NOTE: the ARVO-recorded fixed_commit is a distcheck Makefile change and is not the semantic fix; ground root_cause in the MSan origin + source, and describe the mechanism as missing zero-initialization of the iterator union (not missing validation of coverage records).

suggested_fixes.note: Also correct the wording in fine_trace[step 2].note and source.description/tainted_value_origin.description that call this a 'no well-formedness validation' / 'unvalidated range/glyph records' defect: for an MSan uninitialized-value the precise mechanism is missing initialization of the iterator, not missing validation. Set line to the constructor's line at the vulnerable commit 2dde6c8 (line 856 corresponds to CoverageFormat2::Iter::init in that commit and is a different function).
